8701.full: 1. to search after a thief or theft, search a house , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. in Pass. to be detected , (Demosthenes Orator); with participle, κλέπτης ὢν φωρᾶσθαι (Demosthenes Orator); so, κακὸς [ ὢν] ἐφωράθη φίλοις (Euripides):—;also of things, ἀργύριον ἐφωράθη ἐξαγόμενον money was discovered to be in course of exportation, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8705.lxx: in LXX: Job.20:8 A (חִזָּיוֹן), Isa.28:7 A, Wis.17:15 *
8705.full: φάντασμα, -τος, τό (φαντάζω), [in LXX: Job.20:8 A (חִזָּיוֹן), Isa.28:7 A, Wis.17:15 * ;] = φάσμα, an appearance, apparition (Æsch., al.): Mat.14:26, Mrk.6:49 (see DCG, i, 111b).† (AS)

8706.lxx: in LXX: Est.4:17, Da TH Su 1:55, 4Ma.15:25 א1 *
8706.full: φάσις, -εως, ἡ (φαίνω), [in LXX: Est.4:17, Da TH Su 1:55, 4Ma.15:25 א1 * ;] information, esp. against fraud or other crime: Act.21:31.† (AS)

s: that which causes fright, a terror
8707.full: φόβητρον (LTr., WH, -θρον), -ου, τό (φοβέω), [in LXX: Isa.19:17 (חָגָא) * ;] that which causes fright, a terror: pl. (as always, exc.Isa, l.with), Luk.21:11 (Hipp., Plat.).† (AS)

s: to be a smith, work as a smith, ply the hammer
8715.full: 1. to make of copper or (generally) of metal, to forge , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;Mid. to forge for oneself , (Theognis Elegiacus):—;Pass. to be wrought or forged , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to be a smith, work as a smith, ply the hammer , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ χαλκεύειν the smith's art , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8720.full: perhaps a yellowish bird dwelling in clefts the curlew , (Aristophanes Comicus): χαραδριοῦ βίον ζῆν, of a glutton, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

s: to be driven with storm, tempest-tossed
8731.full: χειμάζω (χεῖμα, winter cold) [in LXX: Pro.26:10 (†) * ;] __1. to expose to winter cold, go into winter quarters. __2. to drive with storm; pass., to be driven with storm, tempest-tossed: Act.27:18.† (AS)

8733.full: 1. a voting or electing by show of hands , (Thucydides) 2. a vote , Lat. suffragium, in plural, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

8737.full: 1. a tortoise , (Homeric Hymns); prov. of insensibility, ἰὼ χελῶναι μακάριαι τοῦ δέρματος oh ye tortoises , happy in your thick skins! (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. like Roman testudo, a pent-house formed of shields overlapping each other like the scales on a tortoise's back , used by storming parties in approaching a city's walls: then, generally, a pent-house for protecting besiegers, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8740.full: of yesterday , τὸ χθιζὸν χρεῖος their yesterday's debt, (Iliad by Homer); ὁ χθ. πόνος yesterday's labour, (Herdotus Historicus); in adverbial sense, with Verbs, χθιζὸς ἔβη he went yesterday , (Iliad by Homer); χθ. ἤλυθες (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;neuter χθιζόν as adverb = χθές, (Homer); so plural χθιζά, see. πρώιζος. (ML)

8743.full: χλαμύς, -ύδος, ἡ [in LXX: 2Ma.12:35 * ;] a chlamys, or short cloak worn over the χιτών (which see): Mat.27:28, 31 (see Tr., Syn., § 1).† (AS)

8744.full: Lat. laena, a large square upper-garment, a cloak, mantle, (Homer); it was made of wool, and worn over the χιτών, thrown over the shoulders, fastened with a pin or brooch περόνη). It is also called φᾶρος by (Homer), and in later Greek ἱμάτιον, Latin pallium. derivation uncertain (ML)

8748.full: χολάω, -ῶ (χολή), [in LXX: 3Ma.3:1 R * ;] __1. to be melancholy mad (Aristoph.). __2. = χολοῦμαι, to be angry: with dative of person(s), Jhn.7:23.† (AS)

8755.full: a place for transacting business, a counting-house , (Plutarch) (ML)

8756.full: to utter oracles, divine , (Aristophanes Comicus) from χρησμολόγος (ML)

8763.full: χρῄζω (χρή) [in LXX Jdg.11:7, 1Ki.17:18 A * ;] to need, have need of: with genitive of thing(s), Mat.6:32, Luk.11:8 12:30, 2Co.3:1; with genitive of person(s) before ἐν, Rom.16:2.† (AS)

8765.full: juice , especially juice produced by decoction or digestion :—;metaphorically, χυλὸν διδοὺς στωμυλμάτων administering a decoction of small talk, (Aristophanes Comicus); χ. φιλίας (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

8766.full: a pot with feet , or a portable stove for putting a pot upon, (Hesiod) (ML)

s: a sheet of paper, made of papyrus strips
8768.full: χάρτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Isa.8:1 A, Jer.36:2, 6 36:23 (מְגִלָּה) * ;] a sheet of paper, made of papyrus strips (see Kennedy, Sources, 42; Milligan, NTD, 10-12; DB, iv, 945 f.): II Jn 12 (Plat., Inscr.).† (AS)

8769.full: χάσμα, -τος, τό (χάσκω, to yawn), [in LXX: 2Ki.18:17 (פַּחַת)* ;] a chasm, wide space: Luk.16:26.† (AS)

8770.full: unripe wheaten groats , as ἄλφιτα are barley-groats, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

8773.g: to sing along with stringed instruments
8773.full: to sing along with stringed instruments

8776.lxx: in LXX chiefly for כָּחַשׁ pi.
8776.full: ψεύδω to deceive by lies; more frequently in the depon. mid, form ψεύδομαι (so always in NT), [in LXX chiefly for כָּחַשׁ pi. ;] __1. absol., to lie: Heb.6:18, 1Jn.1:6, Rev.3:9; οὐ ψεύδομαι, Rom.9:1, 2Co.11:31, Gal.1:20, 1Ti.2:7 with dative of person(s) (Psa.18:45, Jhn.5:12, al.), Act.5:4; before εἰς, Col.3:9; κατά, Jas.3:14 (Hort, in l). __2. Like act., with accusative, to deceive by lies (Æsch., al.): Act.5:3.† (AS)

8779.full: ψιθυρισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ψιθυρίζω, to whisper), [in LXX: Ecc.10:11 (לַחַשׁ) * ;] a whispering; __(a) of secret slander, 2Co.12:20 (Plut.); __(b) of a murmured enchantment, Ec, l.with† (AS)

8780.full: 1. bare , 2. of land, ψιλὴ ἄροσις a bare corn-field, (Iliad by Homer); πεδίον μέγα τε καὶ ψιλόν (Herdotus Historicus): with genitive, γῆ ψιλὴ δενδρέων land bare of trees, (Herdotus Historicus):—; ψιλὴ γεωργία the tillage of land for corn , opposite to γ. πεφυτευμένη (for vines and olives) , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. of animals, stript of hair or feathers, bare, smooth , δέρμα (Odyssey by Homer); ἶβις ψιλὴ κεφαλήν bald on the head, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. generally, bare, uncovered , ψιλὸν ὡς ὁρᾷ νέκυν (Sophocles Tragicus):—;with genitive bare of, separated from , ψιλὴ σώματος οὖσα [ ἡ ψυχή] (Plato Philosophus) b. bare, stript of appendages , ψιλὴ τρόπις the bare keel with the planks torn from it, (Odyssey by Homer); ψ. θρίδαξ a lettuce with the side-leaves pulled off , (Herdotus Historicus); ψ. μάχαιραι swords without other arms , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. οἱ ψιλοί (i.e. τῶν ὅπλων); soldiers without heavy armour, light troops , such as archers and slingers, opposite to ὁπλῖται, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὸ ψιλόν, opposite to τὸ ὁπλιτικόν, (Xenophon Historicus); ψ. ἔχων τὴν κεφαλήν bare-headed, without helmet , (Xenophon Historicus) 6. ψιλὸς λόγος bare language, i. e. prose , as opposite to poetry which is clothed in metre, (Plato Philosophus); also, ψ. λόγος is a mere speech, a speech unsupported by evidence , (Demosthenes Orator) 7. ψιλὴ ποίησις mere poetry, without music , i. e. epic poetry, as opposite to lyric , (Plato Philosophus):—;but, ψιλὴ μουσική instrumental music unaccompanied by the voice , (Aristotle Philosopher) 8. Oedipus seems to call Antigone his ψιλὸν ὄμμα, as being the one poor eye left him, (Sophocles Tragicus) 9. adverb ψιλῶς, merely, only , (Plutarch) (ML)

s: to strip bare of, to strip of
8781.full: 1. to strip bare of hair, (Herdotus Historicus):—; Pass. to become bald , (Hesiod): generally, to be laid bare , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with genitive to strip bare of, to strip of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. generally, to leave naked, unarmed or defenceless , (Thucydides) 4. Pass. also of things, to be stripped off something, τὰ κρέα ἐψιλωμένα τῶν ὀστέων (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

8783.full: to be at the last gasp

8785.full: 1. sand , so called from its loose, crumbling nature (from ψάω); (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;proverbial, ψάμμος ἀριθμὸν περιπέφευγεν (Pindar) 2. ἡ ψ. the sandy desert of Libya, (Herdotus Historicus) Both ψάμμος and ψάμαθος sometimes drop ψ and become ἄμμος, ἄμαθος. (ML)

8786.full: 1. to touch lightly, rub ; 2. intransitive to crumble away, vanish, disappear , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

s: a mere sound, empty sound, noise
8787.full: 1. any inarticulate sound, a sound, noise , (Homer), etc.; of musical instruments, ψ. λωτοῦ, κιθάρας (Euripides) 2. a mere sound, empty sound, noise , (Sophocles Tragicus); ψόφου πλέως, of Aeschylus, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

8794.lxx: in LXX, of a woman who deals pleasantly in order to corrupt, Sir.42:14 *
8794.full: ἀγαθοποιός, -όν = cl. ἀγαθουργός, [in LXX, of a woman who deals pleasantly in order to corrupt, Sir.42:14 * ;] doing well, acting rightly (Plut.): 1Pe.2:14 (Cremer, 8; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
